title: Five principles that didn't stop a war
sources: Agreement between India and China on Trade and Intercourse between Tibet Region and India, 1954

quiz.q: Panchsheel was first set out in an agreement between India and:
quiz.why: Right. The 1954 India–China agreement on Tibet.

review.note: Written and voiced by Claude (AI voices, Kokoro), 8 Nov 2026. Not yet checked by a subject or Hindi editor. Check every number and date against the listed sources.

lines.say: In 1954, India and China signed five principles of peaceful coexistence.
Eight years later, they fought a war.

beats.say: In 1954, India and China signed five principles of peaceful coexistence. Eight years later, they fought a war.

lines.say: Panchsheel was part of a 1954 agreement on trade with the Tibet region.
In 1962, the two countries went to war.

beats.say: Panchsheel was part of a 1954 agreement on trade with the Tibet region. In 1962, the two countries went to war.

lines.say: Respect for each other's territory, non-aggression, and non-interference.
Equality and mutual benefit. And peaceful coexistence.

lines.say: In G-S-two, use it to discuss idealism in foreign policy.
Principles help, but they need power and trust behind them.
